newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER AND BARCELONA DEADLOCKED OVER RONALDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER AND BARCELONA DEADLOCKED OVER RONALDO.

text.p: Internazionale and Barcelona are no nearer to agreeing a transfer fee for Brazilian striker Ronaldo despite four hours of talks at FIFA headquarters in Zurich on Tuesday.
FIFA said last week the world footballer of the year had legitimately bought out his contract with Barcelona for 4.0 billion pesetas ($25.8 million) and was free to move to Inter.
But the two clubs are still haggling over a separate transfer fee which FIFA said must be agreed by Thursday. If the two sides fail to resolve the issue FIFA will impose a price for Ronaldo.
"Our meeting with Barcelona was cordial but our respective positions have not changed substantially," Inter general manager Giacinto Facchetti said on his return to Italy.
"The biggest disagreement between the two sides is in the different interpretations of FIFA's ruling on Ronaldo last week," he said.
Barcelona vice-president Joan Gaspart said the Spanish club have lowered their asking price for Ronaldo and did not rule out a further meeting before the deadline.
Inter maintain, however, that FIFA's decision means they do not have to make any further payment.
A FIFA spokesman said on Tuesday a fee would be imposed by early September if no agreement was forthcoming by the end of this month. He declined to speculate on the size of such a fee.

Whatever the outcome Ronaldo is certain to stay at Inter. The Brazilian has already made a first appearance in the club's famous blue and black stripes -- in a friendly against English champions Manchester United on Sunday.
Almost 50,000 fans turned out at the San Siro but saw Ronaldo in action for only 17 minutes before he was substituted.
